title: Sufi watchfulness
hookLine: Sufi meditation of watchful awareness: keeping watch over the heart, and knowing you are seen

cards: A stranger walks into a gathering around the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him. His clothes are very white, his hair very black, there's no dust of travel on him, and nobody there knows who he is.
He sits down knee to knee with the Prophet and begins asking questions. What is submission? The Prophet answers.
What is faith? The Prophet answers, and the stranger says, you have spoken truly. Then a third question: what is ihsan, doing what is beautiful?

teach.b: The Prophet's answer, in plain paraphrase: ihsan is to worship God as if you see Him, and if you do not see Him, He sees you.
After the stranger left, the Prophet told his companions it was the angel Gabriel, who had come to teach them their religion. Sufis built a practice on that answer, called muraqaba.

The Arabic word carries the sense of keeping watch, the way a guard watches from a wall. And the watching runs both ways. The Qur'an, in Pickthall's translation, says: "Lo! Allah hath been a watcher over you."
In another surah, speaking of the human being: "We are nearer to him than his jugular vein."
So a person in muraqaba sits still and keeps watch over their own heart: which thought arrives, what pulls at them, what settles.
At the same time they hold the awareness of being seen all the way through, by One nearer than their own pulse.
Sufi orders teach it in different ways and stages; some sit with eyes closed and head bowed, some come to it after remembrance spoken aloud has gone quiet. There's no count to keep.
To some ears, being watched sounds like a camera in the corner.

teach.h: ALLAH HATH BEEN A WATCHER OVER YOU.
teach.b: But in the hadith it sits under ihsan, doing what is beautiful, and Sufi teachers read the watching that way: less a camera than the gaze of One who is near.

how: In Sufi orders, muraqaba is a sitting practice of silent, watchful awareness of God and of one's own heart, taught by a shaykh in different forms, sometimes after a session of spoken remembrance.

games.q: a stranger in white sits knee to knee with the Prophet and asks: what is ihsan? what does the Prophet answer?
o: to give to the poor what you can spare.
to worship God as if you see Him; if you don't, He sees you.
to travel in search of knowledge.
games.why: worship as if you see Him, and if you don't see Him, He sees you. Sufis built muraqaba, keeping watch, on that second half.

practice: Sit upright, eyes closed or lowered, and keep watch over your own heart: a thought comes, notice it; a pull toward your phone, notice that too, without chasing anything away or following it.
Then, if you pray, hold the awareness the hadith describes, that you are seen even though you don't see; if you don't, simply let yourself be seen by the quiet around you.

wordCard.voice: Muraqaba. Watchful awareness: in Sufi practice, keeping watch over the heart while holding that God sees. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: watchfulness, keeping watch; a Sufi name for watchful meditation.

carryVoice: Your line: watchful. Attention turned two ways at once: watching, and knowing you are watched. Rest well.
